claim: K(x) is defined only relative to a fixed universal language; the invariance theorem gives an additive constant (compiler size) that can dominate for short objects.
agent_test: Fix one small DSL for rule descriptions; check that rule ranking is stable across two DSL phrasings at equal tokens.

claim: K is not computable, only upper-semicomputable; any practical use is an upper bound from a real compressor or a model code.
agent_test: Never claim an agent rule is 'shortest'; only 'shorter than the alternatives found'.

claim: Practical MDL (two-part code L(model)+L(data|model)) replaces K by computable codes; ideal and practical MDL differ.
agent_test: Rank candidate rules by rule length plus exceptions length (in tokens) versus rule length alone.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Standard compressors give poor K estimates for strings of 50 symbols or fewer (gzip rate 0.966 at 16 bytes vs 0.398 at 1MB); coding-theorem (CTM/BDM) estimates are the alternative.
agent_test: Do not use gzip length to compare short rule texts; compare by exception count or model log-loss instead.
audit_note: The 0.966/0.398 gzip rates are for Audio-8bit data in Yoran et al., not for K estimates of arbitrary strings; the 50-symbol limit comes from Gauvrit et al.

claim: CTM estimates correlate with machine size r=0.83 and with logical depth r=0.41 on the 5-state 2-symbol machine sample.
agent_test: Not agent-testable directly; background for choosing a short-string complexity proxy.

claim: Children's random-string production (N=68, age ~8.7) is only slightly above random strings in CTM complexity: 21.74 vs 21.46; no grade effect (F(2,65)=0.68, eta2=0.11).
agent_test: Weak: one sample, short strings, in-house measure. Do not build design on it.

claim: Subjective randomness tracks natural-scene statistics (r=.75) more than algorithmic complexity (r=.52) in a re-analysis; the complexity coefficient is small.
agent_test: If humans prefer simple rules, the preference is partly from priors, so an agent simplicity bias needs its own validation.

claim: NCD clustering works on mtDNA (24 species, S(T)=0.996; this measures tree fit to the distance matrix, not correctness) and music (6 errors), robust across compressors.
agent_test: Background; compression distance can group candidate answers, but cost vs embedding clustering is untested.

claim: The gzip+kNN text classifier of Jiang 2023 is inflated: fair tie-breaking cuts accuracy up to 9 points, and a bag-of-words distance beats gzip by +1.4 points (6 of 7 sets).
agent_test: Warns against compression-based results without a trivial baseline; apply to any compression claim for the agent.

claim: LLMs compress many modalities better than specialised codecs when used as arithmetic coders (Chinchilla 70B: ImageNet 43.4%, LibriSpeech 16.4%, enwik9 8.3% raw), but the parameter-adjusted rate is 21.9% on text and about 185-229% on non-text.
agent_test: Raw compression hides model size; any compression metric for the agent must count the scaffold's own tokens.
audit_note: Table columns scrambled in PDF extraction; abstract-level 43.4%/16.4% and 21.9% adjusted confirmed, non-text adjusted rates 185.3/228.9/224.7 appear in the table.

claim: LLM compression ratio predicts benchmark score linearly (Pearson -0.93 overall, -0.95 per domain, RMSE 3.1%; 31 LLMs, 12 benchmarks); a follow-up finds it is the tail of a log curve for code (r=-0.956).
agent_test: Correlational across models; cannot rank scaffolds. Test: does per-item solution description length (tokens) correlate with correctness at equal tokens?

claim: LLMs often fail to write short programs that regenerate data: GPT-4o fails 40% and Llama-3.1-405B 78% on natural 128-byte sequences; GPT-4o accuracy 6.5% on text, 35.6% on 16-bit audio, 33.3% synthetic.
agent_test: Ask the agent for the shortest rule and verify by execution; measure exact-match rate at equal tokens versus chain-of-thought.

claim: Trained program-generating models (SeqCoder) reach 84.5-92.5% on in-distribution synthetic sequences but near zero (<=0.1%) on natural audio, DNA and text for the larger models; over 99% of failures err in the first 16 characters (10K examples).
agent_test: Distribution-shift warning: learned program compressors do not transfer; not directly agent relevant.

claim: Correct LLM programs on natural data are mostly repetition (>95%); chain-of-thought changed accuracy by -1.3 (Llama 8B), -5.1 (70B), +2.1 (405B); execution feedback gave modest gains.
agent_test: Test whether an execute-and-check loop beats chain-of-thought for rule finding at equal tokens.

claim: Neural nets and LLMs have a simplicity bias: pre-trained GPT-2/GPT-3 give exponentially higher probability to low-complexity sequences, stronger after pretraining.
agent_test: Simplicity bias is already in the model, so a 'shortest rule' instruction may add little; test with and without it.

claim: Prequential-code training makes in-context learners prefer simpler functions and generalise better with little data; the advantage vanishes at large data.
agent_test: Training method, not scaffold; boundary: low-data only.

claim: Transformers and LSTMs trained on universal-machine data approach optimal Solomonoff-style predictors on simple sources; regret rises with generating program length.
agent_test: Background; prediction cost scales with source program length.

claim: LLMs do not behave as Solomonoff approximators: 26 checkpoints (0.8-35B) never stay within 3.32 bits of a Krichevsky-Trofimov mixture bound (best trails 4.5 bits at 24 symbols, median 36.5, worst 128).
agent_test: Wan & Mei (b23, d01) has no Solomonoff-style test, only low-confidence few-shot selection (SMS Qwen 3B 76.62 to 90.07, gain near zero at 7-8B, no random baseline). Only c19 has verified numbers, and it is negative. Treat the LLM-as-Solomonoff-approximator claim as unsupported.

claim: MDL-style search solves part of ARC without pretraining: CompressARC 20% of 400 eval and 34.75% of training puzzles (2 guesses, ~20 min/puzzle); MADIL 7% on the ARC Prize 2024 private set, 82% generalisation of found solutions.
agent_test: Compare MDL-ranked candidate programs against majority vote at equal tokens on ARC items; the ARC portfolio is the honest control. Search found no published equal-token comparison of MDL ranking against majority vote on LLM-sampled ARC programs (d10, d14); Greenblatt-style filter-then-vote is the baseline.

claim: LLMs given ontology-induction tasks fail to choose the simplest hypothesis: accuracy falls from >80% at height 1 to <50% at height 2 for all but GPT-4o; strong accuracy very low at height 4.
agent_test: Direct test of whether the agent picks the simplest consistent hypothesis; add a simplicity-check step and measure. Reasoning prompts (CoT, buffer-of-thought, 8 demos) did not close the weak/strong gap; SFT on Qwen3-4B raised strong accuracy +11.0 (h1) to +1.5 (h4). No plain-words parsimony prompt arm and no replication found.

claim: Entropy and K disagree on individual strings: entropy is a property of a distribution, K of an individual object; '110011011111' has entropy .811 but higher K5 than the alternating string.
agent_test: Do not substitute token entropy for rule simplicity.
audit_note: K5 is a Coding Theorem Method estimate, not K itself.

claim: Within a question, shorter reasoning chains are more often correct: shortest vs longest chain math accuracy 63.4 vs 28.9 (LN-Super-49B), 60.0 vs 37.8 (R1-32B), 71.1 vs 56.7 (QwQ-32B), 83.3 vs 58.9 (R1-670B); short-3@k beats majority vote at equal thinking-token budgets.
agent_test: Among k sampled solutions to a rule-induction item, prefer the shortest that passes all examples; compare with plain majority vote at equal total tokens. Caveat: unfinished chains were excluded and the task was math, not rule induction.

claim: LLM in-context accuracy falls with the minimal description length of a concept (operator count 1 to 5): Pearson r from -0.854 to -0.961 across 4 models (n=5 class means; 90% to 74% for Qwen2-72B).
agent_test: Use a small fixed grammar; check that item difficulty for the agent rises with rule length before using length as a ranker.

claim: Human concept difficulty is proportional to Boolean complexity (Feldman 2000, 41 concept types), but rival theories (Vigo 2013 GIST) claim better predictions and say the minimal-formula measure misses the canonical SHJ order; Lafond 2007 is reported to show non-minimal rules.
agent_test: Do not assume shortest-rule preference is how people reason; full text of Feldman 2000 and Lafond 2007 still unread.

claim: Hypothesis-then-program prompting beats direct prompting on 100 ARC problems with GPT-4 (17% direct, 23% program only, 30% summarised to 8 hypotheses, 33% human-selected), but compute is not equalised and no arm selects by rule length.
agent_test: Run the equal-token control: one shortest-consistent-rule step vs the same tokens spent on plain chain-of-thought, on an ARC subset and List Functions.

claim: For program-search by LLM, held-out validation error is a strong selector (LLM-PV: 100% test accuracy from 200 examples on 10-parity, CAP and IsPrime, where SGD stays near 50%); length is not ablated.
agent_test: Rank candidates by held-out example error first and rule length second; test whether length adds anything after validation error.

claim: Coding theorem and invariance theorem as stated in secondary text: |-log2 m(s) - K(s)| < c; BDM upper-bounds K only up to additive terms and degrades toward Shannon entropy. Founding papers (Solomonoff 1964, Kolmogorov 1965, Chaitin 1966, Levin 1973) remain unopened.
agent_test: None; background. No independent 2020-2026 critique of CTM/BDM was found.
